caseno: Writ Petition No. 4646 of 1997 with Writ Petition No. 4648 of 1997.
lawyer:
Habibul Islam Bhuiyan with Moqbul Ahmed for SS Halder, Advocates --- For the Petitioner. 
Zakir Hussain Mazumder, Advocate --- For the Respondent Nos. 2-6.
parties:
Abdul Mazid (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Secretary, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resource, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Secretariat and ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The Rule Nisi issued in Writ Petition No. 4646 of 1997 calls in question the order contained in Memo Nos. বি উ বো/(৩:পৃ)৩/এ-১৮/৯৫-dated 22-6-97 (Annexure-K) issued by the respondent No. 6. The case of the petitioner in the above Writ Petition, in brief, is that the petitioner is a Diploma Engineer (Electrical) and he joined in Power Development Board on 9-12-77 as Sub-Assistant Engineer in Dhaka Zone at System Control Centre and he having remained in this post served in many places being transferred from time to time and lastly, he has been working as Resident Engineer at Nakla Electric Supply, Sherpur, However for reasons best known to the authority, the petitioner by memo dated 1-11-96 (Annexure-B), was suspended from his service. Thereafter by notice dated 22-1-96 (Annexure-E) the petitioner was asked to show cause as to why disciplinary action should not be taken against him as he obtained only 47.78 marks out of 100 marks in the Reward and Punishment Scheme of Power Development Board. The petitioner submitted reply (Annexure-F) stating, inter alia, that the inhabitants of the area concerned are mostly agriculturist and they can not pay the bills of electricity regularly and further the defaulters could not also be traced and moreover, a sum of Taka 21,43,940.63 remained outstanding from government offices. The said explanation not being found satisfactory, Charges (Annexure-G) was framed against the petitioner under Rule 138(a) and (c) of the Bangladesh Power Development Board (Employees) Service Rules. 1982 wherein it was maintained that during the period between July, 1993 to June, 1994 the petitioner obtained in total only 47.78 marks which shows that he was inefficient. The petitioner gave reply (Annexure-H) to the said charge stating, inter alia, that most of the electric lines of the area composed of bamboo posts and joint wires and those lines stretched to remote areas and so it was impossible to stop pilferage of power and further a sum of Taka 21,43,940.63 remained outstanding from government offices and many consumers are untraced for which a sum of Taka 4,77,181.54 remained outstanding and so he is not guilty of the charge. Thereafter, the respondent No.5 issued order dated 21-8-96 (Annexure-I) asking the petitioner to show cause why he should not be dismissed from the service as per Rule 143(4) of the said Service Rules of 1982 and then the petitioner should cause (Annexure-J) stating, inter alia, that target could not be achieved in spite of his best efforts and a sum of Taka 21,43,943.63 remained outstanding from government offices only, which was not his fault. Thereafter the respondent No.6, by impugned order dated 22-6-97 (Annexure-K), dismissed the petitioner under Rule 139(1)(h) of the Service Rules, 1982. 

 3. The Rules Nisi in Writ Petition No.4648 of 1997 calls in question the impugned order contained in Memo Nos.199 বি উ বো/(৩:পৃ)৩/এ-১৮/৯৫-dated 22-6-97 (Annexure-K) to the writ petition issued by the respondent No.6. The case of the petitioner in the writ petition, in brief, is that the petitioner is a Diploma Engineer (Electrical) and he joined in Power Development Board on 21-8-78 as Sub-Assistant Engineer Construction Division Narayanganj, and he having remained in this post served in many places being transferred from time to time from one place to another and lastly has been working as Sub-Assistant Engineer. Distribution Division, Jamalpur, However, for reasons best known to the authority, by memo dated 1-11-96 (Annexure-B) the petitioner was suspended from his service. Thereafter by notice dated 22-1-96 (Annexure-E) the petitioner was asked to show cause as to why disciplinary action should not be taken against him as he obtained only 44.47 marks out of 100 marks in the Reward and Punishment Scheme of Bangladesh Power Development Board. The petitioner submitted reply (Annexure-F) stating, inter alia, that the distance of 11 KV line from Islampur to Jamalpur is about 40 kilometre so due to voltage drop, there is technical loss and moreover 14 Distribution Transformers of his area have been repaired on many occasions which caused system loss and further since 95% wires of the electrical line are open and fixed on bamboo poles which also caused further system loss. The said explanation not being found satisfactory, charge (Annexure-G) was framed against the petitioner under Rule 138(a) and (c) of the Bangladesh Power Development Board (Employees) Service Rules, 1982 (Annexure-G) wherein it was mentioned that during the period between July, 1993 to June, 1994 the petitioner obtained in total only 44.47 marks which shows that he was inefficient. The petitioner gave reply to the said charge reiterating his stand taken in the reply to the show cause, Thereafter the respondent No.5 issued order dated 21-8-96 (Annexure-I) asking the petitioner to show cause why he should not be dismissed from the service as per Rule 143(4) of the said Service Rules, 1982 and then the petitioner showed cause (Annexure-J) reiterating his earlier stand taken in reply to the show cause. Thereafter, the respondent No.6 by impugned order dated 22-6-97 Annexure-K dismissed the petitioner under Rule 139(i)(h) of the Service Rules, 1982. 

 7. Mr Bhuiya further submits that since clauses 3-6 of the above Reward and Punishment Scheme prescribed for mere suspension in respect of the employees who scored below 50 marks, the order of dismissal on the above ground is also illegal and without jurisdiction, Further, the offence described in the show cause notice does not come within the purview of ''misconduct'' as per Rule 138(c) of the Service Rules of 1982. Lastly, charge was framed on 12-3-96 and order of dismissal was passed on 22-6-96, i.e. beyond the period of 3 months as provided in rule 143(4) and so the punishment awarded under Rule 139(i)(h) is illegal and without lawful authority. 

 18. Regarding the submission of Mr Bhuiyan that as per provisions of Rule 143(4) of 1982 Rules, the enquiry proceeding has to be completed within 3 months, a Division Bench of this Court while deciding similar issue under Reward and Punishment Scheme in Writ Petition No. 1845 of 1996 on 2-13-98 relying on the case of Monirul Huq vs Government of People''s Republic of Bangladesh reported in 38 DLR 391, held that in the absence of any consequence in Rule 143(4) of the Bangladesh Power Development Board (Employees). Service Rules 1982, this provision for completing enquiry proceeding within .3 months as contained therein, is not mandatory but directory 

 19. It appears that in both the Writ petitions explanations were called for in terms of Rule 143(1) and since the reply given by the petitioners were not found satisfactory, Inquiry Officers were appointed in terms of Rule 143(3) and the concerned Inquiry Officers, afforded personal hearings to the petitioners and after due inquiry found the petitioners guilty and so this Court, under Writ Jurisdiction, cannot sit as a court of appeal and decide whether the said enquiry officers, on proper appreciation on evidence, duly came to the aforesaid findings. Since it appears that all the relevant procedure of Service Rules of 1982 were followed and the enquiry officers, after giving all opportunities as provided is Service Rules of 1982 and also complying with the provisions of natural justice, found that the charge against the petitioners have been proved, and thereafter, the competent authority after considering the findings of the enquiry officers and other circumstances passed the impugned orders, we are of the view that no interference is called for in these Writ Petitions.
